root.name: Modern Defense: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Polish Variation
root.moves: 1. Nf3 c5 2. c4 g6 3. d4 Bg7 4. e4 Qb6

overview: White builds the broad e4-d4-c4 centre against the Modern set-up, and Black hits it at once with ...Qb6 (or the Pterodactyl ...Qa5+) and the ...c5 break. Black wants to trade White's d-pawn and live on the dark squares around a fianchettoed bishop on g7. The game is a manoeuvring fight over the centre rather than a forced one, and Black's early queen gives White tempi to gain.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the e4-d4-c4 centre and gain tempi against the queen with Nc3, Be2 or Nbd2
Meet ...cxd4 with Nxd4 and play for a Maroczy-type bind
Castle and use the space to restrict Black's pieces

black_ideas.idea: Undermine d4 with ...c5 and trade it off
Use the queen on b6 or a5 to pressure d4 and b2
Complete the ...Nf6 and ...O-O set-up around the g7 bishop

typical_structures.structure: Maroczy bind after ...cxd4 Nxd4 (pawns c4 and e4)
Open c-file with c5 traded for White's d-pawn

character.notes: The early queen sortie makes the middlegame unbalanced, but nothing is forced and neither king is attacked early.

gambit.notes: Pawns are level in the main lines; 4...Qb6 may allow 5.Nc3 and tension on d4 but no pawn is offered for good.

soundness.notes: Sound but with a tempo cost for Black; White is usually described as slightly better.

structure.notes: After ...cxd4 Nxd4 White has c4 and e4 against Black's d6 and e7 pawns, a semi-open game on the c-file.

approach.notes: Played by strong players occasionally as a Modern/Pterodactyl choice, not a system.

level.notes: Few forced lines, but handling the early queen and the Maroczy bind takes judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Pterodactyl Declined/Accepted
sublines_that_differ.how: The queen goes to a5 with check instead of b6 and the lines are more forcing.

character.reason: The early queen makes play unbalanced but not forcing, so neither Solid nor Sharp fits.

gambit.reason: No pawn is given up on purpose in the main line.

soundness.reason: It is slightly worse for Black at most, not refuted.

structure.reason: After ...cxd4 the Maroczy-style centre gives Black a half-open c-file.

approach.reason: Strong players pick it now and then, which is standard rather than offbeat.

level.reason: It asks for judgement about the centre rather than long memorised lines.

plans.reason: Black lets White build the centre and attacks it with c5 and the queen.
